To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dielectric anomalies are detected in the incommetsurate phase of thiourea doped with urea and that the memory effect is detected.
the complex dielectric constant of urea-doping thiourea single crystal shows a series of quasicontinuous anomalies in the inhomogeneously modulated phase.
the dielectric anomalies in the modulated phases of urea-doping thiourea are related to the memory effect and the dielectric constant is strongly influenced by the modulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dielectric properties of the modulated phase.
the study of the dielectric properties of the modulated phase.
the study of dielectric properties of thiourea single crystals doped with urea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in urea-doped SC(2)H(4)N(2) the modulated structure is not affected by the doping.

the modulated structure is not stable enough to be preserved by doping and that the memory effect is a consequence of the fact that the system is not able to follow the temperature changes fast enough to reach the thermodynamic equilibrium.
the dielectric memory effect is due to the slow dynamics of the modulated wave, which is not a pure thermal effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the memory effect in the incommesurate phase is a very sensitive tool to detect the presence of defects.
the modulated state of the urea doped thiourea is a very sensitive system for the study of dielectric anomalies in the vicinity of the incommensuration.
the dielectric constant is strongly dependent on the modulation wave, the temperature and the frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
incommensurate structures are not stable and can undergo a transition to a new phase.
the memory effect in the incommencurate phase of thiourea is very sensitive to the temperature sweep rate.
the memory effects in the modulated phases of thiourea-based compounds are very sensitive to the external conditions.
